1.overview: After David returns to Ziklag, an Amalekite reports Saul and Jonathan’s deaths and claims he killed Saul; David mourns with his men, then orders the messenger executed for killing the LORD’s anointed. David laments Saul and Jonathan in the Song of the Bow, recalling their strength and calling Israel and the mountains of Gilboa to mourn.

sections.heading: David mourns and executes the messenger
The Song of the Bow introduced
David’s lament for Saul and Jonathan

2.overview: David settles in Hebron, where Judah anoints him king, and he sends a message of blessing to the men of Jabesh-gilead for burying Saul. Abner establishes Ish-bosheth as king over Israel, and fighting between Abner’s men and David’s servants at Gibeon ends with Asahel’s death, a truce, and heavy losses.

sections.heading: The Pursuit Ends and the Dead Are Buried

3.overview: David grows stronger as the conflict with Saul’s house continues, while the chapter lists his sons born in Hebron. After Ish-bosheth accuses Abner, Abner offers to bring Israel to David; Joab later kills him, and David publicly mourns his death and denies responsibility.

4.overview: After Abner’s death, Ish-bosheth and Israel lose courage; the account identifies Rechab and Baanah and recounts Mephibosheth’s injury. Rechab and Baanah kill Ish-bosheth and bring his head to David at Hebron, where David orders their execution and has Ish-bosheth’s head buried in Abner’s tomb.

5.overview: All Israel’s elders make a covenant with David at Hebron and anoint him king, and he captures Jerusalem, establishes the City of David, and builds his kingdom with support from Hiram of Tyre. When the Philistines attack, David seeks the LORD’s direction and defeats them twice, first at Baal-perazim and then from Gibeon to Gezer.

6.overview: David brings the ark of God toward Jerusalem, but Uzzah dies after touching it, and David leaves the ark at Obed-edom’s house. After hearing that the LORD blesses Obed-edom, David brings the ark into the City of David with celebration, and Michal criticizes his dancing before the LORD.

sections.heading: Uzzah and the Ark at Obed-edom’s House
The Ark Enters the City of David

7.overview: After settling in his palace, David tells Nathan that the ark remains in a tent, and Nathan initially approves his plan to build a house for God. God tells Nathan that David will not build the temple, promises to establish David’s house and kingdom through his descendant, and David responds with a prayer of praise and petition.

8.overview: David defeats the Philistines, Moabites, Hadadezer of Zobah, the Arameans, and the Edomites, establishing control over their lands and receiving tribute. He dedicates captured wealth to the LORD, while the chapter records his just rule over Israel and names his officials.

9.overview: David asks whether anyone from Saul’s house remains so he can show kindness for Jonathan’s sake, and Ziba identifies Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth in Lo-debar. David brings Mephibosheth to Jerusalem, restores Saul’s land to him, and appoints Ziba’s household to manage it while Mephibosheth eats continually at the king’s table.

sections.heading: Land and a Place at the King’s Table

10.overview: David sends condolences to Hanun, but Ammonite officials accuse his servants of spying, and Hanun humiliates them; the Ammonites then hire Aramean allies. Joab and Abishai rout the Ammonite and Aramean forces, and David defeats Aramean reinforcements at Helam, prompting Hadadezer’s subject kings to submit to Israel.

sections.heading: Joab and Abishai Defeat the Allies
David Defeats the Arameans at Helam

11.overview: While Joab leads Israel’s siege of Rabbah, David remains in Jerusalem, takes Bathsheba, Uriah’s wife, and learns that she is pregnant. After Uriah refuses to go home, David arranges his death in battle, brings Bathsheba into his house after her mourning, and the LORD judges David’s actions as evil.

sections.heading: David’s Attempts to Conceal the Pregnancy

12.overview: Nathan confronts David with a parable about a rich man who takes a poor man’s lamb, then declares that David has despised the LORD by taking Uriah’s wife and arranging Uriah’s death; David confesses, and Nathan announces both forgiveness and consequences. The child born to David and Bathsheba dies despite David’s fasting, Solomon is born and named Jedidiah, and David joins Joab in capturing Rabbah and subduing the Ammonite cities.

sections.heading: Nathan Rebukes David and Announces Judgment
The Child’s Death and Solomon’s Birth

13.overview: Amnon follows Jonadab’s advice to lure Tamar to him, then rapes her and sends her away; Tamar grieves in Absalom’s house, while David is angered and Absalom silently hates Amnon. Two years later, Absalom has Amnon killed at a sheep-shearing feast, flees to Geshur, and remains there as David mourns and longs for him.

14.overview: Joab sends a wise woman from Tekoa to present a case about a threatened heir, and she uses it to challenge David for leaving Absalom banished, invoking God’s way of making room for the banished. David orders Joab to bring Absalom from Geshur to Jerusalem but bars him from the king’s presence; after two years, Absalom compels Joab to arrange a meeting, and David receives him.

sections.heading: The woman’s plea for her son

15.overview: Absalom wins Israel’s support through public appeals and launches a conspiracy at Hebron, prompting David to flee Jerusalem with his household and followers. David sends the ark back with Zadok and Abiathar, learns that Ahithophel has joined Absalom, and directs Hushai to return to Jerusalem and counter the conspiracy.

16.overview: Ziba meets David with provisions and claims that Mephibosheth expects Israel to restore his grandfather’s kingdom, and David transfers Mephibosheth’s property to Ziba. At Bahurim Shimei curses and pelts David as the king refuses Abishai’s offer to kill him; meanwhile, Absalom enters Jerusalem, receives Hushai, and follows Ahithophel’s counsel to publicly take his father’s concubines.

17.overview: Ahithophel urges Absalom to pursue David immediately, but Hushai recommends gathering all Israel for a larger campaign, and Absalom accepts Hushai’s counsel as the LORD turns Ahithophel’s advice aside. Hushai’s warning reaches David through Jonathan and Ahimaaz, David crosses the Jordan, Ahithophel dies by suicide, and the opposing forces assemble in Gilead as supporters bring provisions to David at Mahanaim.

sections.heading: David Receives Warning and Crosses the Jordan
Ahithophel Dies and David Receives Aid

18.overview: David organizes his forces under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, remains behind at the people’s request, and orders them to spare Absalom. David’s army defeats Israel in the forest of Ephraim, Joab kills Absalom despite David’s order, and the messengers report the victory as David grieves for his son.

19.overview: After Joab confronts David over his mourning for Absalom, David sits at the gate and Judah brings him back across the Jordan as king. Shimei seeks pardon, David hears Mephibosheth’s account and divides his land with Ziba, Barzillai declines to go to Jerusalem in favor of Chimham, and a dispute between Judah and Israel breaks out over who has the greater claim to David.

20.overview: Sheba son of Bichri leads Israel in revolt against David, while Judah remains loyal; back in Jerusalem, David confines the concubines left in the palace and sends Amasa to summon Judah. Joab kills Amasa and pursues Sheba to Abel-beth-maacah, where a wise woman negotiates the city’s surrender of Sheba’s head, and the chapter concludes with David’s officials listed.

21.overview: A three-year famine leads David to learn that Saul’s killing of the Gibeonites has brought bloodguilt on Israel; the Gibeonites request seven of Saul’s descendants, and David delivers them while sparing Mephibosheth, after which Saul and Jonathan are buried and God answers the land’s prayers. The chapter then recounts four battles with the Philistines in which David’s men kill four descendants of Rapha, while David is rescued from Ishbi-benob and told not to fight again.

22.overview: David sings to the LORD, recounting his cry in distress, the LORD’s dramatic intervention, and his rescue from powerful enemies. He declares his integrity, celebrates the strength and victories the LORD gives him over enemies and nations, and concludes with praise for the LORD’s salvation and lasting devotion to David’s line.

sections.heading: David’s Integrity and the LORD’s Ways
Praise for Salvation and Lasting Devotion

23.overview: David’s final oracle identifies him as the LORD’s anointed, describes just rule in the fear of God, affirms God’s everlasting covenant with his house, and compares the worthless to thorns. The chapter recounts the exploits of David’s mighty men, including the Three, Abishai, and Benaiah, and names the Thirty and their companions.

24.overview: The LORD's anger against Israel leads David to order a census, which Joab questions before completing it across the land; after receiving the troop count, David confesses his sin. Through Gad, the LORD presents David with three judgments, sends a plague that kills seventy thousand, then stops it at Jerusalem, where David builds an altar on Araunah’s threshing floor and the plague ends.

sections.heading: The Census of Israel and Judah
David’s Altar at Araunah’s Threshing Floor
